create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

oidc_jwt.description: When a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Default & special scopes
oidc_jwt.note: This broadens claims by design; tests for least privilege must request explicit narrow scopes.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens require offline_access in both provider configuration and request.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Authorization code / Refresh token grant / Create OAuth2 provider
oidc_jwt.note: Missing refresh_token is expected unless offline_access is configured and requested.

oidc_jwt.description: A token can only be introspected from the same provider used to authenticate, unless first exchanged for a token from the target provider.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > OAuth introspection endpoint
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-provider introspection failure is expected and not an audience-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: The email_verified claim now defaults to False unless customized by scope mapping.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Email scope verification; Provider property mappings
oidc_jwt.note: Applications expecting email_verified=true may fail by design unless a custom mapping sets it.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer authentication for machine-to-machine login is documented as signature/expiry validation, without documented jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > JWT authentication
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid JWT may succeed by design; do not flag as replay vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens require offline_access to be configured and requested.
oidc_jwt.source: add-secure-apps/providers/oauth2/index.mdx#authorization-code
oidc_jwt.note: Missing refresh_token is expected unless offline_access is enabled on both sides.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-based machine-to-machine authentication creates service accounts derived from provider name and token subject, and externally issued JWTs can yield multiple service accounts depending on subject values.
oidc_jwt.source: add-secure-apps/providers/oauth2/machine_to_machine.mdx#jwt-authentication
oidc_jwt.note: Identity materialization as service accounts is expected behavior for this flow and should be considered when interpreting subject-to-identity mappings.

oidc_jwt.description: Automatically generated service accounts for client_secret-based automatic service account creation follow the naming scheme ak-<provider_name>-client_credentials.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Automatic service account creation
oidc_jwt.note: Provider-added prefixes/suffixes in resulting identities are expected and should not be flagged as identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay testing, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT bearer assertion as a vulnerability by itself. The docs describe JWT authentication as validating signature and expiration, and do not document jti tracking or one-time-use semantics for JWT bearer input tokens. replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti are BY DESIGN hardening checks here, not security failures.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > JWT authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests against login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack token. The docs state that input JWTs are checked for signature trust and exp validity; a failed attack login without a control cannot distinguish expired/nbf rejection from broken provider/source configuration.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For expired_token tests on externally issued JWTs, set exp to {{now_epoch_minus_N}}. authentik explicitly rejects input JWTs whose exp is set to now or in the past. Do not use exp={{now_epoch}} as a valid boundary case; it is documented as expired.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > Externally issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 trust-anchor and key-rotation tests, the fuzzer MUST configure a trusted OAuth Source JWKS/Well-known URL and select that source in the OAuth2 provider before using login_with_jwt. Without selecting Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers, JWT bearer authentication is not enabled and failures are not evidence of signature validation.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs; OAuth Source > JWKS

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 trust_anchor_substitution tests, do NOT assume issuer is validated by default for externally issued JWTs. The docs only guarantee signature trust against selected source certificates and exp checking; issuer restriction must be enforced separately via an Expression policy using request.context["oauth_jwt"]["iss"]. A test that omits such policy cannot claim issuer-validation success.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > Externally issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 alg_none, resign_attacker_key, and kid_injection tests, use login_with_jwt via client_assertion and assert rejection at /application/o/token/. The accepted trust model is 'signed by any of the selected sources/providers certificates'; unsigned tokens or tokens signed by attacker keys outside the selected trust set must be rejected. Do not test these attacks through /userinfo or introspection because those endpoints validate output tokens, not the consumed input JWT.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > JWT authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, after changing the trusted JWKS/Well-known/source selection, perform a NEW login_with_jwt request. The docs state source discovery/JWKS data is fetched and stored on save, with no automatic re-fetching for OAuth Sources. A valid coherence test must update the saved source/provider configuration, then verify old-key JWTs fail on subsequent logins.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source > Well-known/JWKS; Machine-to-Machine authentication > JWT authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change sequences, treat new logins under updated provider/source configuration as the expected behavior. A valid stale-config test must show that a JWT signed by key-A succeeds before rotation and fails after rotation on a fresh token request; it is NOT a bug that authentik applies the new configuration to new logins immediately.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source > Well-known/JWKS; Machine-to-Machine authentication > JWT authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 scope tests, when no scope is requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore, to test least-privilege or scope escalation, the fuzzer MUST send an explicit narrow scope set. Omitting scope will broaden claims by design and causes false positives.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Default & special scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 refresh-token and offline-access tests, note that starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive an access token by default. To obtain a refresh token, both the provider configuration and the request must include offline_access. Absence of a refresh token without offline_access is by design, not a bug.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Authorization code / Refresh token grant / Create OAuth2 provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request explicit initial scopes and compare exchanged-token claims against that original scope set. Because authentik defaults missing scope to all configured scopes, a baseline token obtained without scope is already maximally broad and cannot detect escalation.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Default & special scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 introspection tests, you are only able to introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, or you must first exchange the token for a token from that provider. Cross-provider introspection failures are expected and must not be reported as audience-binding bugs.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > OAuth introspection endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: For redirect_uri_mismatch and general OIDC code-flow tests, authentik validates redirect URIs against the provider's configured Redirect URI list, and those entries may be regex patterns rather than exact strings. Tests must distinguish exact configured URIs from regex-allowed URIs; a redirect accepted by a configured regex is by design, not a mismatch bypass.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC request-object tests, the docs provided do not document request-object signature enforcement or a requestObjectSignatureAlg-style setting. You may still send the request parameter to /application/o/authorize/, but any result must be treated as undocumented behavior unless corroborated elsewhere; do not over-interpret acceptance/rejection as a documented guarantee.
oidc_jwt.source: Authorization endpoint glossary; OAuth 2.0 provider endpoints table

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token revocation cleanup, use /application/o/revoke/ with form-encoded token and client authentication parameters. Do not assume revocation is admin-global; it is an OAuth client operation tied to the provider/client context.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider endpoints table; Revocation endpoint glossary

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay_same_token on oidc_jwt, DO NOT flag reuse of the same JWT client assertion as a vulnerability based on documentation alone. The docs only state that externally issued JWTs must be signed by configured sources and not expired, and that authentik-issued JWTs must be valid, not revoked, and not expired; they do not document jti tracking or one-time-use semantics for JWT bearer assertions.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack token. The docs state only that input JWTs are checked for signature trust and that exp must not be now or in the past; without a control, a generic token-endpoint error cannot be distinguished from broken provider/source configuration.

For I1 trust-anchor and key-rotation tests on login_with_jwt, the fuzzer MUST configure a Federated OIDC Source with either Well-known URL, OIDC JWKS URL, or raw JWKS data, and then select that source in the OAuth2 provider. JWT authentication only trusts keys from selected Federated OIDC Sources or configured federated providers; testing without this setup is invalid.

For I1 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, remember that OAuth Source discovery/JWKS fetching happens upon saving the source and 'No automatic re-fetching is done.' After changing the upstream JWKS or discovery document, the fuzzer MUST re-save/update the source/provider configuration before expecting new trust anchors to take effect.

For I1 alg_none and resign_attacker_key tests on login_with_jwt, use the client assertion form parameters exactly: grant_type=client_credentials and client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer with client_assertion=<JWT>. Sending the JWT in unrelated parameters is not the documented JWT-auth path and may produce false negatives.

For I5 scope tests on exchange_code_for_token and token_exchange, when no scopes are requested authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore, to test least-privilege and scope escalation correctly, the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit narrow scope set; omitting scope broadens claims by design.

For I5 refresh-token expectations, starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive an access token by default. To receive a refresh token, both the application/provider configuration and the request must include offline_access. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token as a bug unless offline_access was configured and requested.

For I2 authorization-code freshness tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. Replay tests for code reuse should target exchange_code_for_token with the same code twice; replay expectations should not be transferred to JWT bearer client assertions or access tokens unless separately documented.

For I3 config-change tests involving redirect URIs, authentik validates redirect_uri against the provider's configured Redirect URI list, and that field may contain regular expressions. A test is only valid if the same redirect_uri is used across baseline and attack requests unless the test intentionally targets redirect validation; otherwise regex-based acceptance can confound results.

For I3 redirect-uri tests, an empty Redirect URI configuration on a newly created OAuth2 provider causes authentik to save the first URL a user opens that app with as the redirect URL. The fuzzer MUST preconfigure redirect URIs explicitly before testing redirect_uri_mismatch or related coherence properties; otherwise first-use auto-registration changes behavior by design.

For I5 token introspection, the docs state you are only able to introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, or you must first exchange the token for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests in the same provider context as the token under test, otherwise failures are by design.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience / token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use token_exchange on /application/o/token/ with explicit audience and subject_token parameters. Because the docs do not specify subject_token audience-validation semantics, the fuzzer SHOULD compare exchanged-token claims and acceptance behavior carefully and treat results as implementation findings, not setup failures.

For I4 identity verification, compare the sent identity primarily against the UserInfo sub claim. The docs do not document a platform-added display_name prefix pattern for OIDC UserInfo responses, so no prefix-stripping heuristic should be applied.

For I5 email-claim tests, note the documented version behavior: prior to 2025.10, the email scope always set email_verified=True; as of 2025.10, email_verified defaults to False unless customized by scope mapping. Do NOT flag this version-dependent claim value as an authorization-binding bug without accounting for provider version and custom mappings.

For I1 JWT trust tests, login_with_jwt only validates input JWTs against JWTs signed by selected Federated OIDC Sources or configured Federated OIDC Providers. The fuzzer MUST first create/configure a trusted OAuth source or provider and bind it to the OAuth2 provider under test; otherwise issuer/key-substitution tests are meaningless because no external JWT trust path exists.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token tests against login_with_jwt, authentik explicitly checks that the input JWT exp claim is not now or in the past. The fuzzer MUST include a control login using a valid token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} to distinguish expected expiry rejection from broken provider/source configuration.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti, do NOT flag reuse of the same externally issued JWT as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation only requires signature validation and exp freshness for external JWTs, and for authentik-issued JWTs requires valid access token, not revoked, not expired. No jti replay tracking is documented for JWT bearer login.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, OAuth source discovery/JWKS data is fetched and stored when the source is saved, and no automatic re-fetching is done. The fuzzer MUST perform an explicit source update/save when rotating keys or discovery metadata; merely changing the remote JWKS will not update authentik trust state.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source -> OpenID Connect -> Well-known / JWKS

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change sequences involving provider or application access changes, authentik outposts update immediately via websockets when associated app/provider config changes. A valid stale-config test must show old credentials still accepted after the update, not just that a new login under new config behaves differently.
oidc_jwt.source: Outposts -> Any change made to the outpost's associated app or provider immediately triggers an event to update the configuration data stored on the outpost, via websockets.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 jwt_default_role_change analogs on authentik OAuth scopes, when no scopes are requested authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. The fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope set when testing authorization narrowing/broadening; omitting scope can silently broaden claims and create false I5/I3 results.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Default & special scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 scope tests, refresh tokens are only returned when both the application/provider is configured with offline_access scope mapping and the request includes offline_access. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token as a bug unless both sides requested offline_access.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Authorization code / Refresh token grant / Create OAuth2 provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 empty_audience-style tests on OAuth scopes/claims, when a client does not request any scopes authentik behaves as if all configured scopes were requested. The fuzzer MUST NOT use an empty or omitted scope request as a 'minimal privilege' baseline; explicitly request the intended scopes instead.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Default & special scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 token introspection tests, authentik only allows introspection of a token from the same provider used to authenticate, unless the token is first exchanged for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspect_token with matching provider credentials or perform token exchange first; cross-provider introspection failures are by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> OAuth introspection endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation and cross-provider exchange tests, token_exchange uses the same /application/o/token/ endpoint and behavior depends on provider/application configuration. The fuzzer MUST bind the correct application/provider and explicitly set audience and scope in the exchange request; otherwise failures may reflect provider mismatch rather than audience/scope enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider endpoints table + token endpoint glossary + machine-to-machine authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: Redirect URI matching is not exact-string-only: authentik can validate against a configured list of redirect URIs, and administrators may use regular expressions. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the provider is configured with a literal URI or regex; a URI that differs textually may still be valid by regex and is not an I3 failure.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC request object tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), the authorization endpoint supports an optional request JWT parameter, but the provided docs do not specify request-object signature enforcement settings. The fuzzer SHOULD test unsigned request objects, but MUST interpret acceptance cautiously because documentation does not state whether request object signing is configurable or required.
oidc_jwt.source: Task-required standard OIDC endpoint extraction + authorization endpoint docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For login_with_jwt, the client_secret parameter can alternatively carry the input JWT for compatibility. The fuzzer MUST distinguish this compatibility path from normal client_secret authentication when interpreting results; acceptance via client_secret=<inputJWT> is by design, not a secret-validation bypass.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
